sections.h2: Ways to sell a Colleyville home
sections.html:
An investor with cash will close on the day you choose. A regular listing in a city of costly houses takes more time and can pay more. Colleyville owners usually weigh both.

The city is in northeastern Tarrant County, and almost every household owns its home. Investor rentals are scarce here, and the usual house is big and long held.

  • Cash purchase: the buyer accepts the house in present condition, so you skip showings and loan approval.
  • Listing: best for a house in good shape, at the cost of inspections and repair haggling.
  • Private sale: possible if you have a written contract and a title company to run the closing.

Colleyville is wealthy and stable. As of July 1, 2025 the city counted 25,727 people, 1.2% fewer than in April 2020, spread over 9,072 households averaging 2.86 people. About 94.1% of residents stayed put for a full year, so few houses reach the market.

sections.h2: What to collect before you list
sections.html: Closing needs paper, so dig it out early: the deed, your newest appraisal notice, proof of a homestead or over-65 exemption, and a tax certificate. A house that came through an estate also needs the court order, executor's letters or a recorded deed naming the person who may sign. Folders assembled in advance save days between contract and funding.

Tarrant County mails bills near October 1. Pay by January 31 and nothing extra accrues. On February 1 a penalty of 6 percent begins and grows each month until it reaches 12 percent in July, and interest of 1 percent monthly runs alongside.

Come July 1, unpaid accounts pass to tax attorneys, whose fee can add as much as 20 percent. Anyone splitting the bill in two pays November 30 and June 30. Older and disabled owners may spread payments over a quarterly plan from January through July. Exemption filings at Tarrant Appraisal District close April 30, and protests close May 15.

sections.h2: Filing a homestead exemption with Tarrant Appraisal District
sections.html:
Filing costs nothing. Use the district's online form, or print form 50-114 and mail or email it. A Texas driver's license or ID card carrying the home address is required.

A buyer who moves in gets the exemption from that date, as long as the previous owner had not claimed one that year. It also holds yearly appraisal growth to 10 percent, except for improvements and added land.

Inherited property needs extra documents: an ownership affidavit, the earlier owner's death certificate, a current utility bill and the citation of any court record. Other heirs who live in the house must each sign an authorization.

Many Colleyville owners are old enough to hold a school tax ceiling, which freezes the school bill on their homestead. Those 65 or older also get an extra $60,000 school exemption. The ceiling can move with you to a new Texas homestead, and a surviving spouse aged 55 or more keeps it. Ask the district, before listing, how a transfer would work for you.

At closing, the year's bill is divided between you and the buyer. The lien forms each January 1, which leaves the owner on that day liable. Back taxes come out of your proceeds at the closing table. Request a tax certificate from the county before you accept an offer, so the figure holds no surprises.

sections.h2: Can heirs sell a Colleyville house quickly?
sections.html: Yes, as soon as title is clean. Probate of a will is available for four years after a death. The small estate affidavit covers estates up to $75,000, leaving out the homestead. Heirs might also use a muniment of title, an executor's deed, or a transfer on death deed that the owner recorded while alive. A plain heirship affidavit is just a sworn statement, so some buyers decline to rely on one.

A servicer in Texas typically holds off until the loan is over 120 days behind. After the default notice you have 20 days to catch up. A sale notice then precedes the first-Tuesday auction by at least 21 days. Sell the house before that Tuesday and the auction is cancelled.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited or downsized house
sections.html:
Many sales here follow a move to smaller quarters or a death in the family. First confirm whose name is on title and who may sign. Then collect the original will, if one exists, a list of every heir and the recorded deed.

Next, ask the title company which documents it will insure on. One may close on a court order alone, another may insist on a recorded transfer on death deed or an executor's deed. Answering that question before buyers call keeps a deal from collapsing late.

Colleyville's median owned home is valued at $784,900 and median rent is $3,263. At that level, small flaws shift the price a long way. A financed buyer will order an appraisal and an inspection, and either report can reopen the price talk.

Keep receipts for roof, HVAC, foundation and plumbing jobs, along with permits for any additions. A tidy maintenance file reassures buyers and gives you a firm reply to a low offer.

Before signing anything, get three answers in writing. Is the offer price firm after the walkthrough? Who pays for the title policy and recording? What is the target closing date, and may you stay a few days past it while the movers finish? A buyer who answers plainly is usually one who closes.

sections.h2: How a cash sale unfolds here
sections.html:
A cash buyer tours the house, typically once, then puts an offer on paper. If you agree, the title company searches records, requests lender payoffs and drafts the deed, and you sign on the date you picked. Because big, long-held houses often need updating, the buyer will discount for roofs, kitchens and mechanical systems, so the offer will sit under a fully staged listing price.

In return you get certainty: no loan can fall through, no appraisal can come in short and no showings disturb the household. For an owner relocating, settling an estate or dodging months of carrying costs on an expensive house, that can justify the discount. Line up written offers by what you would net.

faqs.q: Is selling without an agent common in Colleyville?
faqs.a: It can, for a sound house when you can manage showings and contracts yourself. The title company still drafts the deed and divides the tax year.

faqs.q: When does a Colleyville buyer get the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: From the move-in date, when the seller had not claimed one that year.

faqs.q: Where is a Colleyville protest filed?
faqs.a: At Tarrant Appraisal District, by May 15 for the current year.

faqs.q: What if taxes on a Colleyville house are late?
faqs.a: Penalty rises each month to 12 percent in July, with 1 percent interest monthly on top. Get the payoff from the county; closing normally clears it.

faqs.q: Can an heir sign a Colleyville deed before probate ends?
faqs.a: Seldom. A buyer's title company wants a court order, executor's authority or a recorded transfer on death deed first.
